title: The Massive 55 Percent Drop in US Births

scenes.narration: Have you noticed families look different today than they did decades ago?

visual.text: The Massive 55 Percent Drop in US Births

scenes.narration: Back in 1960, the US fertility rate was 3.65 births per woman.
By 2024, that number plummeted to just 1.63.
That is a staggering 55% decline in birth rates over those decades.
The full story is on the channel.

visual.text: A massive demographic shift is reshaping our future.

title: Is the US Birth Rate Finally Rebounding?

scenes.narration: Are we finally seeing a rebound in American birth rates?

visual.text: Is the US Birth Rate Finally Rebounding?

scenes.narration: The data shows a small glimmer of change recently.

visual.text: Minor shifts tell a deeper story.

scenes.narration: Between January 2023 and January 2024, the fertility rate ticked up by 0.6%.
However, this follows years of decline, including a 1% drop from 2020 to 2024.
The full story is on the channel.
Why are families getting smaller compared to the mid-nineties?
In January 1995, the fertility rate was 1.98 births per woman.
Today, that rate has fallen by 18%.
Economic pressures and new life goals are making smaller families the modern norm.
The full story is on the channel.
